newsitem.title: DENMARK: Ukraine's Ukrgazprom denies stealing Russian gas.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Ukrgazprom denies stealing Russian gas.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 12, Reuter - Ukraine's Ukrgazprom has flatly denied stealing gas from Russia following a direct accusation from Russian Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev.
"We now transport 120 billion cubic metres (bcm) through Ukraine. It used to be 110 bcm. Ask them about it - they've stolen gas from us for several years and sold it on to others," said Vyakhirev.
Not so, says Ukrgazprom. Bogdan Klyuk chairman of the board, told a news conference on Thursday that Ukraine does no such thing.

"If there is such an accusation, then I think Gazprom should sue us in a court," he said. He added that Ukrgazprom continued to sign monthly contracts with Gazprom, and "we have had no controversy so far."
Gas transit is Ukrgazprom's biggest business, with revenues for carrying Russian gas standing at $2.5 billion a year, although Klyuk said that profits were "rather lower."
In 1994, he said, Ukrgazprom carried 95 bcm of Russian gas, rising to 107 bcm in 1995 and 117 bcm in 1996.

Klyuk said that Ukrgazprom has signed a joint venture with Russia to transport 30 bcm a year to Turkey, and would also be supplying Bulgaria with 1.3 bcm a year within four years to settle debt following an inter-governmental agreement. --Sebastian Alison, Copenhagen Newsroom, +45 33 96 96 50
